findings.title: The per-candidate L-BFGS-B polish spends 6.3% of the sweep's gradient evaluations on results it throws away
findings.claim: Over the 51 stress.sweep_combinations() solves, 149 of 206 _lbfgsb_restart polishes are discarded (the function returns its input), and those discarded polishes take 1,200 of 18,967 gradient evaluations (6.3%). 24 of them end ABNORMAL at nit 0 after 501 gradients (about 21 each) without making any progress. Each gradient is one 96-row simulate_trajectory_batch.
findings.mechanism: _multi_start_minimize polishes every solved candidate (#1208) by restarting L-BFGS-B at full maxiter from that candidate's own converged point, with a fresh Hessian and scipy's default maxls=20. When the candidate already sits at a line-search-flat point, the first line search runs all 20 trials, and each trial evaluates the supplied batched jac. The run returns status 2 (ABNORMAL), nit 0, and x unchanged. Other polishes converge to a drop below _LBFGSB_RESTART_KEEP_REL and are rejected. The per-scenario share of discarded polish work is highest on the cheap single-zone solves (median 13.1%, max 41.6%).

null_control.note: Flat prices do not remove the effect (0.0783, with 34 ABNORMAL nit-0 polishes costing 714 njev). The waste is a property of the restart and not of the price structure, which is expected for an overhead claim. The perturbation arm is the discriminating test

findings.proposed_fix_scope: optimizer.py:_lbfgsb_restart only. Use a cheaper line-search budget or an early exit for the polish, for example a projected-gradient check at best.x before restarting. It must be proved against D0's polish-gap grid (#1208) that no adopted polish is lost. Pi extrapolation, an assumption: a Pi 4 runs about 4x slower than this x86 box, so the 4.8 % CPU share is about 0.2 s of a 4.4 s x86 two-zone DHW solve, or about 0.8 s per cycle on a Pi. The cost is bounded and falls in the worker process, not on the loop.

findings.title: In-process fallback solve starves the event loop 65-90% of its wall time despite _gil_yield (provisional)
findings.claim: When a real coordinator cycle solves in-process (the fallback taken when the worker is unusable), the event loop's 1 ms heartbeat sees gaps over 5 ms during 65-90% of the executor-busy wall time, with a maximum gap of 30-46 ms. The shipped process route shows 29-32% and an idle loop shows 8-9% under the same load. The _gil_yield docstring's claim that it is 'exactly the yield a loop's 1 ms heartbeat needs' does not hold, because the batched gradient (one simulate_trajectory_batch, about 6 ms of CPU per call on this box) contains no yield.
findings.mechanism: _gil_yield runs once per memoized scalar objective call. A gradient is one vectorised batch call with no yield inside it, and scipy calls the jac at every line-search trial, so most of the solve's wall time is spent in stretches longer than CPython's 5 ms switch interval. The loop thread wakes for its tick and then waits up to one switch interval for the GIL.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: optimizer.py only: yield inside the batched gradient (per jac call, or per step of simulate_trajectory_batch). This is scoped low because the fallback is non-default and capped at WORKER_FALLBACK_CAP=3 consecutive cycles (coordinator.py:641). Pi extrapolation, an assumption: at about 4x slower per step each hold is about 4x longer (about 25 ms per gradient).
